S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder defined by persistent disturbances such as delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking, disorganized or catatonic behavior, and negative symptoms, with associated decline in functioning. Its course often unfolds gradually, with social or occupational deterioration becoming clearer over months to years, and it is distinguished from brief psychotic disorder, delusional disorder, and mood disorders with psychotic features by its duration, breadth of impairment, and lack of primary mood-episode explanation.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient.stressor: When Bruce Foster’s consulting firm asked him to lead a larger environmental modeling contract and supervise two additional junior analysts, the change disrupted the steady routines that had long helped him balance demanding data work with hiking, astronomy, and volunteering. Over the next 2 years and 2 months, his long-standing tendency to double-check work hardened into fixed beliefs about the project and people around it, while his motivation, expressiveness, and interest in colleagues, STEM mentoring, and star-gazing meetups steadily diminished. The impairment became clinically significant when he could no longer complete modeling deliverables reliably, stopped mentoring staff, and withdrew at home despite his wife’s efforts to keep their routines intact. He entered psychiatric care after his primary care physician, initially consulted for work-related decline and increasing isolation, referred him for a psychiatric evaluation.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because I’m pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and planting errors in the datasets to make it look like I can’t lead the work, even when my wife or the junior analysts tell me it’s just version-control mistakes.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: These days I can sit for hours at my desk or in the garage with the telescope still covered, knowing I used to enjoy hiking, mentoring the younger analysts, and going to astronomy nights, but I just don’t feel much pull to start anything or talk to anyone.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve fallen far enough behind on the modeling deliverables that my firm reassigned pieces of the contract, and I’ve stopped being useful to the junior analysts I’m supposed to supervise. At home, I mostly keep to myself and my wife has had to push me just to keep basic routines going.
add_requirements.duration: This whole decline started after I was put in charge of the larger environmental modeling contract about two years and two months ago.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The certainty that people on the project are tracking my revisions and planting errors has been there for about the last two months.
